question.text: A sample of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>mg</mi></math> of an unknown monohydric alcohol, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>OH</mi></math> was added to methylmagnesium iodide. A gas is evolved and is collected and its volume measured to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math>. The molecular weight of the unknown alcohol is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>mol</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Alcohols on reaction with Grignard reagent forms hydrocarbons.This is due to the presence of active hydrogen in alcohols and here grignard reagent acts as a base.

When any alcohol is treated with methyl magnemsium iodide the hydrocarbon formed should be methane gas.

ROH+CH3MgI→ROMgI+CH4g

Number of moles of CH4= Number of moles of ROH
